pamphlet_excerpts: Outdoor Activities Gardening: Like all outdoor activities, gardening has itsrisks.
Start Dressing Appropriately: You can start by dressing appropriately forgardening, for instance, jeans, boots, gloves, hat, and a long-sleeved shirt for protection.
Frequently Apply Sunscreen: To ward offsunburn, frequently apply sunscreen with an SPFof at least 15.
Least Prepared Forthe: You should at least be prepared forthe following.
step_by_step_procedure: Treat Minorcuts Scrapes: Treat minorcuts and scrapes by flushing the area with cleanwater for at least five minutes to wash away foreignmatter.
Rusty Nails Sharp: Rusty nails, sharp sticks, andbroken glass could cause a puncture wound.
Thesewounds Difficult Easily: Thesewounds are difficult to clean and are easily infected.
Flush Out Dirt: Help flush out dirt or particles by irrigating the area with clean, running water for about five minutes.

pamphlet_excerpts: Growing Seed Fun: Growing from seed is fun because you can watch the entire lifecycle of a plant.
Sprout Germinate Seeds: It is best to sprout, germinate, seeds indoorsin small pots or from seed-starting kits.
Startingseeds Indoors Chance: In addition, startingseeds indoors gives you the chance to see your plants severaltimes a day.
Garden Chance Surviving: Your garden has a better chance of surviving outdoorsif you plant seedlings that already have roots.
step_by_step_procedure: Map Garden Your plants: When youare ready to plant, use the map of your garden to place your plants in the areas you planned.
Show Others Hardyou: You can show others how hardyou worked and what you learned.
Garden Contests Atcounty: You might find garden contests atcounty and state fairs, county extension services, farmers’ markets, andlocal garden clubs.
Read Gardensection Local: Read the gardensection in your local newspaper tofind out about garden shows.

Probably Aspade Small: You probably will need aspade or small shovel, a hoe, a rake, a yardstick, bamboo or other wooden stakes, and stretchablegarden string.
Want Pair Garden: You also might want a pair of garden gloves to help protectyour hands.
Thrift Stores Hardware: Thrift stores, hardware stores, and discount gardencenters are good places to find garden implements.
step_by_step_procedure: Planning Garden Decide: Before you plantyour garden, Planning Your Garden decide what crops After you have decided what you want to grow, identify which crops grow.
Sometimesyou Plant Crops: Sometimesyou can plant crops that need cooler temperatures beneath thevines or stalks of a taller crop that can tolerate full sun.
Growing Seed Fun: Growing from seed is fun because you can watch the entire lifecycle of a plant.
Sprout Germinate Seeds: It is best to sprout, germinate, seeds indoorsin small pots or from seed-starting kits.

pamphlet_excerpts: Chemical Burn Not: A chemical burn might not be immediately noticeable.
However Long Dry: However, as long as the dry chemical is on the skin, it willcontinue to burn.
Quickly Brush Off: Quickly brush off as much of the chemicalas possible using a gloved hand.
Dilute Exposure: Dilute the exposure bycontinuously flushing the area with water for at least 15 to 20 minutes and seek medical attention.
step_by_step_procedure: Recent Years Scientists: In recent years, scientists have beenconcerned about the declining populations of pollinators, very likely caused by habitat loss.
Care Pesticides Herbicides: Take care in using pesticides and herbicides, and make your garden friendly for pollinators with plants and trees that attract them.
Think Creating Garden: If you enjoy watching wildlife, think about creating a garden friendly for thewildlife in your own backyard.
Adding Feeders Foodsources: Adding feeders and other foodsources makes a garden even more irresistible for wildlife.

requirements.lead_text: Do ONE of the following and record weekly observations. Discuss the results of your project with your counselor.
requirements.req_text: Do ONE of the following and record weekly observations. Discuss the results of your project with your counselor. (a) Build a compost bin and maintain it for 90 days. (b) Build a vermicompost bin (worm compost bin) and maintain it for 90 days. (c) Build a hydroponic garden containing three vegetables or herbs, or three ornamental plants. Maintain this garden through harvest or flowering, or for 90 days. (d) Build one water garden, either in a container (at least 12 by 6 inches and 6 inches deep), or in the ground as a small, decorative pond no larger than 6 by 3 feet and 24 inches deep. Maintain the water garden for 90 days. (e) Prepare a honey super for use on a hive or colony. Remove a filled honey super from the hive or colony and prepare the honey for sale. (f) Grow a garden of your own using soil from seed or plantings to harvest or for 90 days, whichever is earlier. This can be an outdoor garden or indoors using appropriate containers, and should include at least three types of plants approved by your counselor.
